videos.script: Lesson 16 built a server by hand. Today the same two applications go into images, and one file starts them all. {{title}} A Dockerfile copies the lock file before the code, so an edit to a view does not reinstall every package. {{layers}} The first question to the image finds a gap. psycopg needs libpq, and the slim image has none. The binary extra brings its own. {{libpq}} Then compose. Two databases, Redis, the web, the worker, the clock and the API, in one file, with the secrets beside it. {{compose}} The API does not start. The container found a bug the virtual machine had hidden: a development package the application really needs. {{bug}} Data survives the containers, in volumes. And migrations run once, as a step of their own, before the new code starts. {{release}} That leaves agenda running three ways: on a laptop, on a server under systemd, and as containers. Each built on the one before.
